correctness.rationale: Every derivation equals f(t)∂_t, with f(0)=0 if the truncation length is odd. In characteristic two the square D_f^2 is a derivation and equals zero exactly when f f'=0 mod t^n. For v=ord_t f, the latter is equivalent to vanishing of odd-index coefficients c_j with j≤n-v, while rank is min(m,ceil((n-v)/2)). Sorting the only possible valuations for each rank produces explicit coordinate charts: punctured affine plane times affine space for r≤floor(m/2), and multiplicative times affine space for larger ranks. The arithmetic point-count formula follows. Independent direct polynomial multiplication and matrix Gaussian elimination checked all 17 finite q,n cases in the packaged Python script. The computations do not certify the universal argument; the derivation identities prove it.

originality.rationale: The statement classifies the reduced rank loci of square-zero Leibniz derivations on all single-variable power truncations in characteristic two and proves adjacent-length isomorphisms. Avramov–Buchweitz–Iyengar classify differential-module phenomena for arbitrary R-linear square-zero operators (not Leibniz maps); Premet treats regular derivations in characteristic >2; Skryabin studies nilpotent derivations in prime-truncated multivariable Jacobson–Witt algebras. Direct comparisons and semantic searches revealed no theorem implying the present rank-specific geometric and finite-field distributions. Absence in searched sources is not absolute priority proof.

value.rationale: Square-zero derivations are differential structures with Leibniz compatibility, and their ranks determine homology size. The result classifies the intrinsic reduced rank-locus geometry for every length in characteristic two, gives an explicit half-rank transition from punctured-plane to toric affine strata, and establishes unexpected isomorphism of the full family of rank loci between adjacent even and odd truncation lengths. This is an infinite parametrized geometric classification plus complete finite-field rank distribution, not a single small calculation or a generic all-derivation rank recomputation.
